name: Clinking Glasses
baseMeaning: Two glasses clinking together in a toast.
tldr: 🥂 marks a shared toast: congratulations, celebration, or an invitation to celebrate and drink together.

contextMeanings.meaning: When people are actually raising glasses, 🥂 refers to the toast itself.
contextMeanings.example: we're at the bar, cheers to us 🥂

contextMeanings.meaning: In a dating thread, 🥂 suggests sharing a drink and can serve as a light invitation to meet.
contextMeanings.example: want to get drinks after work? 🥂

contextMeanings.meaning: In a work thread, 🥂 is a warm way to celebrate good news such as a promotion.
contextMeanings.example: Congrats on the new role, you earned it 🥂

contextMeanings.meaning: Used over grief or painful news, 🥂 can appear to dodge the recipient's feelings.

platformNotes.note: 🥂 works in iMessage as a compact celebration marker after a promotion, wedding, or other good-news message. A single glass feels warm; several can make the same moment feel overdone.
In an Instagram caption or comment, 🥂 can turn congratulations into a shared toast. It also works well beside a milestone announcement, including when paired with 🍾.
On TikTok, 🥂 commonly marks the celebration in a comment or caption. The surrounding words determine whether it is a toast, an invitation to meet, or misplaced cheer.
In WhatsApp family and friend threads, 🥂 is an easy way to join a celebration from afar. “🥂 tomorrow?” can also suggest a drink, while a lone glass simply celebrates.

generationalNotes.note: For younger senders, 🥂 often feels immediate and shared: “we did it 🥂” pulls the other person into the celebration. In dating, it can suggest making the toast a shared drink.
Millennials commonly use 🥂 for familiar milestones such as promotions, weddings, birthdays, and New Year's, where a warm and concise congratulations fits.
There is no major generational divide in the symbol itself. Most Gen X readers will understand 🥂 as a toast, with the surrounding words deciding what kind of celebration it represents.

warnings.title: Celebrating over grief
warnings.description: 🥂 in a grief thread can look like an attempt to steer around the pain. Send a sentence that acknowledges what happened instead.

warnings.title: Too much cheer for a small win
warnings.description: A stack such as 🥂🥂🥂 can make a modest accomplishment feel overperformed. Use one 🥂 or a plain sentence that matches the size of the moment.

seoDescription: What does 🥂 mean? It signals a shared toast, congratulations, or an invitation to drink, fitting milestones, promotions, weddings, and friendly gatherings.

longForm.overview:
The first 🥂 is usually a reaction to something worth raising a glass for: a promotion, a wedding, a birthday, a launch, or good news shared in a group chat. The sender often wants the moment to feel communal rather than private. Instead of adding only “congrats,” 🥂 pictures two glasses touching, so the message implies “I am celebrating with you.”

That sets it apart from 🎉, which marks a celebration without showing the drinking ritual. 🥂 can also be a small invitation: “🥂 tomorrow?” suggests meeting for drinks, while a lone 🥂 after a family announcement simply means the sender is joining in from wherever they are. Add 🍾 and the meaning becomes more emphatic, as if a cork were popping for the milestone. The reason being celebrated still matters. In a joyful thread, 🥂 feels warm and shared. In a sad one, it feels like the sender has changed the subject.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🥂 commonly arrives as a bare reaction under good news: “we did it 🥂” after a promotion, or as the final sign-off on a wedding announcement. A single glass is enough when the text already explains the event. Repetition changes the tone: 🥂🥂🥂 can make a modest success feel like a stadium cheer, while 🥂🍾 marks the occasion as a milestone worth making louder.

It also works as shorthand for a plan. “🥂 tomorrow?” is not merely congratulatory; it suggests that the sender wants to meet and drink with the recipient. In dating threads, the same symbol can hint at a drink for two. In family threads, it often says that the sender is celebrating even from a distance.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not send 🥂 when the thread contains grief, disappointment, or serious pain. The glasses will look as if the sender is steering away from the person's feelings, and a celebratory image can make the message feel careless. The same problem appears when the occasion is smaller than the reaction: three 🥂 after a minor win turns sincere congratulations into an over-the-top performance.

Christmas is another place to check the relationship. “merry christmas 🥂” can feel friendly and seasonal to a close friend, but too familiar to a coworker, where a polite sentence or ☕ is safer. The emoji is acceptable for a coworker's promotion, so the issue is the Christmas setting, not work itself. Match the glasses to the moment rather than using them as a default sign-off.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🥂, you can mirror the invitation with “🥂 cheers to you” or name the occasion: “that promotion deserves a toast.” When the message contains a plan, such as “🥂 tomorrow?,” answer the plan directly and suggest a time and place. Two glasses in the reply can emphasize a shared celebration, especially with a romantic partner.

If 🥂 lands on your own good news, treat it as participation rather than a generic reaction. A short “thank you! 🥂” tells the sender you appreciated the warmth. If the glasses feel excessive or slightly off, ask whether they were meant literally; a calm question can turn a misread into an actual invitation. If the thread is serious, do not force a cheerful reply.

faqs.question: What does 🥂 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: In a dating thread, 🥂 often means he wants to toast the good news with you and may be suggesting you meet for a drink. It is not proof of romantic interest, so the rest of the message matters.

faqs.question: Is 🥂 flirty?
faqs.answer: It can be. With a romantic partner, 🥂 may suggest drinks for two; in a dating chat, “🥂 tomorrow?” can be an invitation to meet.

faqs.question: What does 🥂 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it usually means a shared celebration. Depending on the surrounding words, it can celebrate good news, mark a milestone, or suggest meeting for drinks.

faqs.question: Should I send 🥂 to a coworker?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially for a promotion or another genuine win. Send one 🥂 for warmth, but reconsider it in a Christmas message, where it may feel too familiar.

conversationExamples.message: babe wanna get drinks after work? 🥂
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a light invitation to meet and toast the good news together. Respond with a time and place, especially if you are interested.
The sender is sharing a small celebration and wants the group to join in. Congratulate them enthusiastically without turning the thread into a pile of emojis.

conversationExamples.message: hey congrats on the new role, you earned it 🥂
conversationExamples.interpretation: A single 🥂 makes this a warm coworker message rather than a formal announcement. Acknowledge the promotion and wish them well.

conversationExamples.message: mom and dad are celebrating 40 years today 🥂
conversationExamples.interpretation: The glasses mark a family anniversary and let the sender celebrate from afar. Reply with affection or mention the milestone without adding a louder celebration.

conversationExamples.message: new album drops tonight and i can't wait 🥂
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is joining the launch celebration with a shared-toast gesture. Respond with excitement, a congratulations, or your own 🥂 if that feels natural.
